prompt: Find an expression for the nth term of the sequence 29, 36, 43, 50, ...
hint: Work out the difference between the terms first.
explanation: The terms go up by 7 each time, so the nth term starts 7n. When n = 1, 7n = 7, and the first term is 29, so add 22: the nth term is 7n + 22. Check: n = 2 gives 7 × 2 + 22 = 36.
source_ref: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Mathematics (1MA1) content reference A25
